   - Code: `src/routes/webhooks.js:7`.
   - Doc: `TODO_WORKFLOW.md:5` is the only task row and covers "Checkout + order status".

   - Code: `src/routes/webhooks.js:7`.
   - Doc: `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md:4` says "Handles checkout and order status."
   - Fix: add Stripe payment confirmation to the scope line, and point invariant #1's "Enforced at" cell at `src/routes/webhooks.js`.

- **Two helpers are undefined.** `verifyStripeSignature` and `markOrderPaid` (`src/routes/webhooks.js:10`, `:12`) are never imported or defined; the only import is `Hono` (`:2`). - **Item 2:** is the unique constraint on the payment intent id or the session id?
- **Bad-signature response:** the handler doesn't define one, so I'd record it as an open question in the new row rather than guess a status code.
- **Version:** I'd bump `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md:3` from 0.4 to 0.5 (proposed).

# Architect

Design and document the system before building it — in the house doc format,
kept in sync at all times. Output is **documents, not code.**

## Principles

Enforced *in the docs*: **model first** (data + invariants before
framework) · **enforce every invariant at the core**, ideally at *two*
boundaries (app-layer validation **and** a DB constraint) — never "the frontend
handles it" · **design failure paths** as deliberately as happy paths · **small,
reversible, independently shippable steps** · **one source of truth** —
everything else derives from it and links back.

## Proactive use

If a new app, feature, or workstream is starting and no current design docs
exist, invoke this without being asked: announce in one line — "Running
architect: <why>" — and proceed. Never ask permission to run the skill; the 1–3
blocking questions below are still allowed.

## The four artifacts (+ the modular set)

Authority flows top-down. A fact lives in exactly one place and is linked from
everywhere else.

1. **`SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`** (apex) — the canonical, slow-changing truth: scope &
   non-goals · the domain model · the **invariants** and *where each is
   enforced* · the load-bearing decisions as mini-ADRs (*decision · why ·
   alternative rejected*). If anything conflicts with this file, this file wins.
   Keep it tight — it is the contract, not the manual.
2. **`ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`** — architecture + phased plan derived from the
   SoT. Header block (`Version · Status · Owner`), then §-numbered: `0` Executive
   context · `1` Tech stack (Layer · Tech · Role table) · `2` Data schema

## Sync protocol — the docs are never allowed to drift

This is the whole point. Bake it into `CLAUDE.md` and obey it yourself:

  `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` first (if it touches a truth/invariant/decision), then
  `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`, then the affected `docs/architecture/NN-*.md`,
  **then** the code. Never ship a change the docs don't yet describe.
- **One fact, one home, many links.** A detail is defined once and referenced by
  link elsewhere. Every doc header links to the others.
- **TODO tracks reality.** Every task cites the arch §/file it implements; a task
  that changes architecture names the doc it updated; statuses are current.
- **Definition of "synced":** no architectural claim in code that isn't in the

- **No code in this phase.** Pseudocode for a tricky algorithm is fine; an
  implementation is not.
- Every component has a defined responsibility *and* a failure mode.
- Flag unknowns as open questions — never invent a constraint, a number, or an

- A choice you made that the user didn't give (a status code, a limit, fail-open

## 1. Scope

| # | Capability | Source |

| S1 | A signed-in user can have a PDF of one of their trip itineraries **emailed to their own account address**. | (given) |
| S2 | The same PDF can be **downloaded** in the browser. Also the fallback when email fails. | (proposed) — [Q5](#6-open-questions) |

**Non-goals (v1):**

- Sending to anyone other than the caller (no "share by email", no cc/bcc).
- Scheduled or recurring sends; automatic background retries.
- Storing, archiving or listing previously generated PDFs; an "export history" UI.
- Maps, photos or any images in the PDF; custom templates or branding options.
- Other formats (ICS, CSV, DOCX).

- Localised PDFs — one locale and one page format in v1 ([Q6](#6-open-questions)).
- Designing auth or the trip/itinerary model. They are prerequisites — see §2.

## 2. Upstream contract

The repo is empty. This feature **reads** the things below but does not own them. Shapes are the minimum the feature needs — **(proposed)**, pending [Q2](#6-open-questions).

| Upstream | What this feature requires of it |
|---|---|
| Session | `getSessionUser()` → `{ id, email, emailVerifiedAt }` for the signed-in caller, or `null`. |
| `users` | `id` (PK) · `email` · `email_verified_at` (`NULL` = unverified). |
| `trips` | `id` (PK) · `owner_id → users.id` · `title` · `start_date` · `end_date`. |
| `itinerary_items` | `id` · `trip_id → trips.id` · `day` (date) · `start_time`, `end_time` (nullable) · `title` · `location` (nullable) · `notes` (nullable) · `position` (order within a day). |

- Itinerary times are **wall-clock values local to the place**. This feature prints them exactly as stored and never converts time zones.
- If the real upstream model differs, only the snapshot reader changes ([roadmap §3.1](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#31-structure)); nothing downstream of it reads the database.

## 3. Domain model

| Concept | Stored? | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| **ItineraryExport** | Yes — `itinerary_exports` | One row per export attempt (download or email). The **ledger**: sole source for idempotency, single-flight, rate limiting, audit and metrics. Column-level schema: [roadmap §2](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#2-data-schema). |
| **ItinerarySnapshot** | No | Immutable plain-data copy of one trip + its ordered items, read at a single instant. The **only** input to the renderer. |
| **PDF** | No | Derived bytes: `render(snapshot)`. Regenerated on every request, never persisted. |

**Export state machine** (the only legal transitions):

```
              ┌──► succeeded   download: PDF bytes produced · email: provider accepted the message
processing ───┤
              └──► failed      failure_code set — see the failure matrix
```

- A row is inserted as `processing` and committed **before** any rendering or sending.
- `succeeded` and `failed` are terminal. A retry is a **new** export with a new idempotency key.
- "Accepted by the provider" is not "delivered to the inbox". The UI must not claim delivery.
- Failure codes and what the user sees: [roadmap §3.4](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#34-failure-matrix).

| I1 | **Authorised trips only.** An export exists only for a trip the caller may export (v1: the owner — [D6](#5-decisions)). | `canExportTrip` guard before the ledger insert; failure → `404`. | Snapshot query is owner-scoped (`trips.id = $trip AND trips.owner_id = $user`) and is the only read path for export data. *(Query predicate, not a constraint.)* |
| I2 | **Self-only recipient.** Email goes only to the caller's own account address. ## 5. Decisions

| ID | Decision | Why | Alternative rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | **One server-side render path; PDFs are derived and never stored.** (proposed) | One definition of the document for both download and email. No storage, retention policy, stale copies or second place holding personal data. | *Client-side generation* — the email path needs the bytes on the server anyway, and two renderers drift. *Object storage + signed link* — adds infra, expiry and link access control. |
| D2 | **PDF engine: `@react-pdf/renderer` behind a `renderItineraryPdf` port.** (proposed, gated on spike [T0.3](TODO_WORKFLOW.md#phase-0--foundations-and-de-risking)) | Pure JavaScript, so it runs on any Node host including serverless. No HTML is rendered, so no injection or SSRF surface (I11). The port keeps a swap contained. | *Headless Chromium print-to-PDF* — matches the web UI exactly but needs a browser binary, more memory, slower cold starts, and renders user content as HTML. *pdfkit / pdf-lib* — imperative layout, more hand-written pagination. |
| D3 | **Process inline in the request; durable ledger row first; no queue or worker in v1.** (proposed) | The send is user-initiated, self-addressed and low-stakes: immediate "sent" or "failed, try again" beats background retries, and the user is the retry mechanism — made safe by I4 and I5. No new infrastructure. | *Outbox + worker or hosted queue* — adds a process or vendor, a polling UI and more states. **Revisit if** p95 exceeds `REQUEST_BUDGET`, provider flakiness makes manual retry common, or scheduled sends are requested. The ledger already carries what a worker needs. |
| D4 | **Recipient = the caller's verified account email** (given). **Delivered as an attachment** (proposed). | "Email it to themselves." An attachment works offline, which is when an itinerary is needed, and needs no storage (D1). | *Link to a hosted PDF* — needs storage and link authorisation, and fails without connectivity. |
| D5 | **Every export, download or email, is a ledger row.** (proposed) | One mechanism for I4, I5, I6, audit and metrics. | *Ledger for email only* — leaves download renders unmetered (CPU abuse) or needs a second rate limiter. |
| D6 | **Owner-only in v1, behind a single `canExportTrip` guard.** (proposed) | Sharing does not exist yet; one guard is the only place to change when it does. | *Composite FK `(trip_id, user_id) → trips (id, owner_id)`* — a true DB guard, but it breaks on sharing and on ownership transfer. |
| D7 | **Mail provider sits behind a `Mailer` port; provider not chosen.** | No basis yet to pick a vendor (accounts, cost, region) — [Q3](#6-open-questions). The port lets Phase 1 and the dev adapter proceed. | *Calling a vendor SDK from the service* — couples the core to an unmade choice. |

> Do not persist generated PDFs (disk, object storage or database) without an explicit decision here (D1).

**Accepted trade-off (D3).** If the process dies, or the provider call times out, *after* the provider accepted the message but *before* the row is finalised, the row ends as `failed` and a user retry can produce a second identical email. Judged harmless for a self-addressed itinerary. Closing it depends on [Q8](#6-open-questions).

# Architect

Design and document the system before building it — in the house doc format,
kept in sync at all times. Output is **documents, not code.**

## Principles

Enforced *in the docs*: **model first** (data + invariants before
framework) · **enforce every invariant at the core**, ideally at *two*
boundaries (app-layer validation **and** a DB constraint) — never "the frontend
handles it" · **design failure paths** as deliberately as happy paths · **small,
reversible, independently shippable steps** · **one source of truth** —
everything else derives from it and links back.

## Proactive use

If a new app, feature, or workstream is starting and no current design docs
exist, invoke this without being asked: announce in one line — "Running
architect: <why>" — and proceed. Never ask permission to run the skill; the 1–3
blocking questions below are still allowed.

## The four artifacts (+ the modular set)

Authority flows top-down. A fact lives in exactly one place and is linked from
everywhere else.

1. **`SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`** (apex) — the canonical, slow-changing truth: scope &
   non-goals · the domain model · the **invariants** and *where each is
   enforced* · the load-bearing decisions as mini-ADRs (*decision · why ·
   alternative rejected*). If anything conflicts with this file, this file wins.
   Keep it tight — it is the contract, not the manual.
2. **`ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`** — architecture + phased plan derived from the
   SoT. Header block (`Version · Status · Owner`), then §-numbered: `0` Executive
   context · `1` Tech stack (Layer · Tech · Role table) · `2` Data schema
   (low-level: columns, types, constraints, indexes, JSONB shapes, decision
   call-outs) · `3` Backend (structure · services · API-contract table) · `4`
   Frontend · `5` Execution phases · `6` Non-functional requirements.
3. **`docs/architecture/00-index.md` + `01-…NN`** (larger projects only) —
   agent-friendly modular extracts of the roadmap sections. The index carries a
   **File Map** table (# · file · covers · roadmap §), a **Dependency Graph**
   (ASCII), and a **Quick Reference** ("I need to work on X → read these files").
4. **`TODO_WORKFLOW.md`** — the task tracker. Status legend (`[ ]` ·
   `[IN PROGRESS]` · `[FINISHED - PENDING MERGE]` · `[MERGED/DONE]` ·
   `[BLOCKED]`); tasks grouped by phase; each row:
   `# · Task · Architecture Ref (linked to the §/file) · Status · Branch`. A
   task closed mid-phase leaves a `Left for <id>: ...` note for whoever picks
   it up next.
5. **`CLAUDE.md`** (project root) — the rules file Claude Code auto-loads:
   operating rules + the sync protocol (template below). One markdown file — no
   `.clauderules`, no `.cursorrules`, no import shim.

## Sync protocol — the docs are never allowed to drift

This is the whole point. Bake it into `CLAUDE.md` and obey it yourself:

- **Top-down, docs-before-code.** A change to any architectural fact updates
  `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md` first (if it touches a truth/invariant/decision), then
  `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md`, then the affected `docs/architecture/NN-*.md`,
  **then** the code. Never ship a change the docs don't yet describe.
- **One fact, one home, many links.** A detail is defined once and referenced by
  link elsewhere. Every doc header links to the others.
- **TODO tracks reality.** Every task cites the arch §/file it implements; a task
  that changes architecture names the doc it updated; statuses are current.
- **Definition of "synced":** no architectural claim in code that isn't in the
  docs · no dead cross-links · `00-index` File Map matches files on disk · TODO
  statuses match git reality.

## `audit` mode

Given `architect audit`, do **not** author — verify sync and report drift: code

Every drift item cites **both sides**: the `file:line` in code that states the
fact, and the doc (+ § or line) that should describe it and doesn't. No item

## Before you start

Ask 1–3 blocking questions only (scale, users, hard constraints, existing
stack). State assumptions for the rest and proceed — don't stall. Match depth to
size: a single feature → `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH` + a light `ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP` +
`TODO_WORKFLOW` + `CLAUDE.md`; a new product → add the modular
`docs/architecture/` set. An existing doc set that's just missing one fact — a
new invariant, an endpoint, a decision — gets that one addition wired into its
right doc and cross-linked; it does not get re-authored from scratch.

## Rules

- **No code in this phase.** Pseudocode for a tricky algorithm is fine; an
  implementation is not.
- Every component has a defined responsibility *and* a failure mode.
- Flag unknowns as open questions — never invent a constraint, a number, or an
  API you haven't confirmed.
- A choice you made that the user didn't give (a status code, a limit, fail-open
  vs fail-closed, a library) is a proposal, not a fact: mark it `(proposed)` in
  the doc and list it under "Decisions to confirm" in your reply.
- Decision-dense: tables and bullets, not prose. Call out reversed or forbidden
  decisions inline (`> Do not reintroduce X without an explicit decision`).
- Verify or say you don't know; never invent a path, API, number, or fact.
  Commits are the repo owner's alone: no AI co-author trailer, no AI mention in
  messages.

## When not to use

- A small fix or task already covered by current design docs — just do it.
- Pure implementation of an already-designed phase — code, don't re-spec.

## Hand-offs

- Repo with a remote → run `up-to-date` first so the design builds on latest code.
- A load-bearing decision with genuinely competing options → `ask-the-council`
  before locking it into `SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`.
- After a phase is implemented → `review-swarm` the diff before the PR.
- The doc set carries prose a human (not an agent) will read — §0 executive
  context, a README, a mini-ADR rationale → `humanizer` on *those passages
  only*. The tables, invariants, and contracts stay as they are; they're
  reference text, and "sounding human" is not a goal there.

The four docs exist, cross-link, and agree with each other and the planned code;
a competent dev could build from them without guessing the model, the
invariants, the failure handling, or the order — and `CLAUDE.md` makes the sync
protocol non-optional for whoever builds it.

## 2. Domain model

### 2.1 Upstream entities (required, not owned)

The repo is empty, so these do not exist yet. This feature needs only the contract below. Their real shape is [OQ-2](#5-open-questions).

| Entity | What this feature needs from it |
|---|---|
| `User` | A stable id · an email address · a way to tell whether that address is verified |
| `Trip` | A stable id · an owner (a `User`) · a title |
| Itinerary content | The ordered items of a trip, readable in one query scoped to a user |

### 2.2 `ItineraryDocument` (value, not stored)

The read-only snapshot the renderer consumes. It is the **only** seam between the trip model and this feature: one reader produces it, one renderer consumes it.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tripId`, `title` | Identity and heading |
| `dateRange` | Trip start and end, if the trip has them |
| `days[]` → `items[]` | Items grouped by day, in itinerary order. Item fields `(proposed)`: `time?`, `title`, `location?`, `notes?` |
| `generatedAt` | Render timestamp, printed in the PDF footer |

### 2.3 `ItineraryExport` (owned, table `itinerary_exports`)

One row per email export attempt. It is the in-flight marker, the rate-limit ledger, and the audit record. Downloads (S3) create no row. Column-level schema: [ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP §2](ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md#2-data-schema).

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Export id. Also the idempotency key sent to the email provider |
| `user` | Requester **and** recipient. There is no separate recipient attribute |
| `trip` | The trip exported |
| `status` | `processing` → `sent` \| `failed`. Terminal states never change |
| `failureCode` | Set only when `failed` (vocabulary below) |
| `providerMessageId` | Set only when `sent` |
| `createdAt`, `finishedAt` | Request time, and time the row reached a terminal state |

**Status meaning**

| Status | Guarantee |
|---|---|
| `processing` | A request is rendering or sending right now |
| `sent` | The email provider accepted the message. It does **not** mean the message reached the inbox |
| `failed` | The attempt ended without a confirmed send. It does **not** guarantee no email went out: a provider timeout is ambiguous |

| `provider_unavailable` | Provider 5xx, 429, network error, or timeout | Yes |
| `abandoned` | Row was still `processing` after `STALE_AFTER` (request died mid-flight) | Yes |

All `(proposed)`. They are defined here once and live in a single constants module in code.

| Name | Value | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR` | 5 | INV-5 |
| `STALE_AFTER` | 2 minutes | INV-7. Must exceed `RENDER_TIMEOUT + SEND_TIMEOUT` |
| `MAX_PDF_BYTES` | 10 MB | INV-8 |

## 4. Decisions

Every decision here is `(proposed)` until confirmed.

| ID | Decision | Why | Alternative rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | The recipient is never an input. It is derived from the session | "Email it to themselves" is the requirement, and it is also what stops the endpoint being a spam relay | A `to` field validated against the account email: same result, with a bug waiting to happen |
| D2 | Render server-side with a pure-JS PDF library (`@react-pdf/renderer`), in the Node.js runtime | Runs the same on serverless and on a container, no browser binary. Hosting is unknown ([OQ-1](#5-open-questions)) | Headless Chromium: heavy, slow to cold-start, awkward on serverless. Client-side print-to-PDF: cannot be attached to a server-sent email |
| D3 | The PDF is never stored. It is rendered on demand and attached to the email | No object storage, no retention policy, no second copy of user data | Upload and email a link: revisit only if PDFs approach `MAX_PDF_BYTES` |
| D4 | The `itinerary_exports` row is the single record of an export. Terminal states are final. A retry is a new export with a new row | One state machine with no backward edges | A `failed → processing` retry edge: more states to get wrong for no user-visible gain |
| D5 | v1 renders and sends **inside the request**. No queue, no worker | The user is present and watching, so a manual retry is acceptable. Zero new infrastructure. Works on any hosting | A background job queue. Revisit when any of these holds: the request p95 becomes uncomfortable, transient provider failures become a visible support issue, or N3 is lifted. The row already carries what a worker would need |
| D6 | Email goes through an `EmailSender` port with one adapter. Provider: Resend | Keeps the provider swappable and the service testable with a fake | Calling a provider SDK from the service directly |
| D7 | Rate limiting is counted from `itinerary_exports` rows | Postgres is already there. No Redis for one counter | An in-memory limiter (wrong on more than one instance) or a new datastore |
| D8 | A trip the user cannot read returns `404`, not `403` | Does not reveal that the trip exists | `403` |
| D9 | An itinerary with no items is rejected with `422 itinerary_empty` | An empty PDF in the inbox reads as a bug | Render an empty document |

> Do not add a recipient parameter, a recipient column, or a "send to a friend" option without a new decision here. It reverses INV-1.

> Delivery is at-least-once from the user's point of view. After an ambiguous provider timeout the row is `failed`, and a retry may deliver a second copy. That is accepted because the recipient is the requester.

## 0. Executive context

A signed-in user opens one of their trips and asks for the itinerary as a PDF, either downloaded or emailed to their own account address. The server reads the itinerary, renders the PDF in memory, and for email hands it to a mail provider as an attachment. Nothing is stored except one small row per email attempt, which doubles as the duplicate guard, the rate-limit ledger and the audit trail.

Version 1 does the whole job inside the HTTP request. That keeps it to zero new infrastructure and makes it hosting-agnostic, at the price of no automatic retry: if the provider is down, the user sees a clear error and clicks again. The design is deliberately narrow in one place. The request cannot name a recipient, and the table cannot hold one, so the feature cannot be turned into a way to mail other people.

The repo is empty today. Auth and the trip model are prerequisites this feature consumes through a small contract; it does not design them.

## 2. Data schema

One new table. Meaning of each attribute: [SOURCE_OF_TRUTH §2](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#2-domain-model).

### `itinerary_exports`

| Column | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` |
| `user_id` | same type as `users.id` | NOT NULL, FK → `users(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE |
| `trip_id` | same type as `trips.id` | NOT NULL, FK → `trips(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE |
| `status` | `text` | NOT NULL, default `'processing'`, `CHECK (status IN ('processing','sent','failed'))` |
| `failure_code` | `text` | NULL, `CHECK` against the failure-code vocabulary |
| `provider_message_id` | `text` | NULL |
| `pdf_bytes` | `integer` | NULL. Size of the rendered PDF, for observability only |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | NOT NULL, default `now()` |
| `finished_at` | `timestamptz` | NULL |

**Row-consistency `CHECK`** (INV-6): exactly one of these holds.

| `status` | `finished_at` | `provider_message_id` | `failure_code` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `processing` | NULL | NULL | NULL |
| `sent` | NOT NULL | NOT NULL | NULL |
| `failed` | NOT NULL | NULL | NOT NULL |

**Indexes**

| Index | Definition | Serves |
|---|---|---|
| `itinerary_exports_one_in_flight` | UNIQUE `(user_id, trip_id) WHERE status = 'processing'` | INV-4 |
| `itinerary_exports_user_created` | `(user_id, created_at DESC)` | INV-5 count, INV-7 expiry |

**Call-outs**

- There is no recipient or email column, on purpose (INV-1).
  > Do not add one without a new decision in the Source of Truth.
- `status` is `text` + `CHECK`, not a Postgres `ENUM` `(proposed)`: the vocabulary is easier to change in a migration.
- `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both FKs: deleting an account or a trip removes its export rows. A request in flight then finds zero rows to update and logs it (INV-6).
- Table and column names of `users` and `trips` are assumptions until [OQ-2](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#5-open-questions) is answered.

## 3. Backend

### 3.1 Structure

Planned layout `(proposed)`. None of these paths exist yet.

```
src/
  app/api/trips/[tripId]/exports/route.ts          POST  email export
  app/api/trips/[tripId]/itinerary.pdf/route.ts    GET   download
  features/itinerary-export/
    service.ts            orchestration for both endpoints
    repository.ts         every query on itinerary_exports
    itinerary-reader.ts   the only code that reads trip tables
    recipient.ts          getVerifiedRecipient
    pdf/                  ItineraryDocument type, PDF component, render function
    email/                EmailSender port, provider adapter, message builder
    limits.ts             the Limits table from the Source of Truth
  db/                     schema + migrations
```

Route handlers stay thin: session, parse, call the service, map the result to HTTP. They hold no rules.

### 3.2 Components

| Component | Responsibility | Failure mode → handling |
|---|---|---|
| Route handlers | Authenticate, parse strictly, map results to the [API contract](#33-api-contract) | Unknown field or bad `tripId` → `400`. No session → `401` |
| `itinerary-reader` | Build an `ItineraryDocument` for `(tripId, userId)` in a query scoped to that user (INV-3) | Trip missing or not readable → returns nothing → `404`. No items → `422` |
| `recipient` | Return the user's address only if verified (INV-2) | Unverified → returns nothing → `422 email_unverified` |
| `repository` | Expire stale rows, count the window, insert, write the terminal state (INV-4 to INV-7) | Unique conflict → `409`. Terminal `UPDATE` touches zero rows → log and leave the row alone. DB unreachable before insert → `500`, nothing sent |
| PDF renderer | Pure function `ItineraryDocument → bytes`. No I/O (INV-9) | Throws or exceeds `RENDER_TIMEOUT` → `render_failed`. Output over `MAX_PDF_BYTES` → `pdf_too_large` |
| `EmailSender` port + adapter | Send one message with one attachment, pass the export id as idempotency key if the provider supports one (unverified), classify the provider's answer | 4xx → `provider_rejected`. 5xx, 429, network, `SEND_TIMEOUT` → `provider_unavailable` |
| `service` | Run the flow in [§3.4](#34-email-export-flow) and own the order of checks | Any step fails after the row exists → the row is closed as `failed` with that step's code |

### 3.3 API contract

All status codes and the error shape are `(proposed)`. Error body: `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, plus `"export": { "id", "status", "failureCode" }` when a row exists.

| Endpoint | Auth | Request | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/trips/{tripId}/exports` | Session | Body `{}`. No fields are accepted | `201` `{ "id", "status": "sent" }` | `400 invalid_request` · `401 unauthenticated` · `404 trip_not_found` · `409 export_in_progress` · `422 email_unverified` · `422 itinerary_empty` · `422 pdf_too_large` · `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After` · `500 render_failed` · `502 provider_rejected` · `502 provider_unavailable` |
| `GET /api/trips/{tripId}/itinerary.pdf` | Session | None | `200`, `Content-Type: application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: attachment` | `401` · `404 trip_not_found` · `422 itinerary_empty` · `422 pdf_too_large` · `500 render_failed` |

There is no status-polling endpoint in v1. The `POST` response is the outcome ([D5](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#4-decisions)).

### 3.4 Email export flow

Pseudocode. The order matters: everything that can reject cheaply runs before the row exists, and nothing is sent before the row exists.

```
POST /api/trips/{tripId}/exports

 1  user      = session user                               else 401
 2  body      = strict parse, must be {}                   else 400
 3  doc       = itineraryReader.load(tripId, user.id)      none -> 404
 4  doc has no items                                       -> 422 itinerary_empty
 5  recipient = getVerifiedRecipient(user.id)              none -> 422 email_unverified

 6  BEGIN
      take advisory lock for user.id                       (INV-5)
      expire this user's rows: processing, older than STALE_AFTER
          -> failed / abandoned                            (INV-7)
      count this user's rows created in the last hour
          >= RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR                           -> ROLLBACK, 429
      insert row (processing) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
          no row returned                                  -> ROLLBACK, 409  (INV-4)
    COMMIT                                  # lock released, row marks the attempt

 7  pdf = render(doc) within RENDER_TIMEOUT                fail -> close(render_failed), 500
 8  pdf larger than MAX_PDF_BYTES                          -> close(pdf_too_large), 422
 9  result = emailSender.send(recipient, message(doc), pdf, key = export.id)
      accepted                -> close(sent, providerMessageId), 201
      rejected (4xx)          -> close(provider_rejected), 502
      5xx / 429 / network / SEND_TIMEOUT
                              -> close(provider_unavailable), 502

close(...) = UPDATE ... WHERE id = export.id AND status = 'processing'   (INV-6)
             zero rows -> log; the row was expired or deleted meanwhile
```

Known gaps, accepted in v1:

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Provider accepted the mail but the response was lost or timed out | Row is `failed / provider_unavailable`; the user may retry and get a second copy |
| Email sent, then the `close(sent)` write fails | Row stays `processing`, later becomes `failed / abandoned` although mail went out. This is why `failed` carries no "nothing was sent" guarantee |
| Process dies between step 6 and step 9 | Row stays `processing` and blocks that (user, trip) until `STALE_AFTER`, then expires on the user's next request |

The download endpoint runs steps 1, 3, 4, 7 and 8, then streams the bytes. It writes no row.

### 3.5 Email message

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| To | The verified account address from step 5. Nothing else |
| Subject | Built from the trip title: CR/LF stripped, length capped |
| Body | Short plain-text and HTML note naming the trip. The itinerary itself is only in the attachment |
| Attachment | One PDF. Filename is an ASCII slug of the trip title plus `-itinerary.pdf` |

Sender address, exact wording and the caps are not decided ([OQ-3](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#5-open-questions)).

---

## 4. Frontend

One control on the trip's itinerary page. It is convenience only; every rule is enforced by the server.

| Element | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| "Download PDF" | Plain link to the `GET` endpoint |
| "Email me the PDF" | Label shows the destination address from the session. `POST`s with an empty body |
| Pending | Button disabled, progress indicator, state announced to assistive tech |
| Success | Confirmation naming the address |
| Failure | Message chosen by `error.code`; "try again" offered for `provider_unavailable`; a "verify your email" link for `email_unverified`; the wait time for `rate_limited` |
| Unverified account | Button disabled with an explanation, instead of letting the request fail |

---

## 5. Execution phases

Each phase merges and ships on its own.

| Phase | Delivers | Depends on | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Groundwork | App scaffold with pinned versions, answers to OQ-1 to OQ-3, a proof that the PDF library renders inside a Route Handler on the pinned Next.js | Nothing | A Route Handler returns a real PDF locally and on the target hosting |
| 1. PDF + download | `ItineraryDocument`, the reader, the renderer, the `GET` endpoint, the download link | Phase 0, a readable trip model, sessions | A user downloads their own itinerary; another user's trip is a `404` |
| 2. Email | Migration, repository, service, `EmailSender` + adapter, the `POST` endpoint, the button | Phase 1, verified-email signal, provider account and sending domain | A user receives the PDF; every row of the failure tables in §3 is covered by a test |
| 3. Hardening | Structured logs and metrics, an alert on failure rate, an end-to-end test, a review of the limits against real usage | Phase 2 | An operator can answer "did export X send, and if not why" from logs alone |

Not planned: background processing, delivery webhooks, link-based delivery. Each needs a decision in the Source of Truth first.

---

## 6. Non-functional requirements

No numeric targets are set. There is no usage data to base them on ([OQ-6](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#5-open-questions)).

| Area | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Security | INV-1 to INV-3 hold under direct API calls, not only through the UI. Trip titles are sanitised before use in the subject and filename. Provider credentials live in server-side environment variables |
| CSRF | The `POST` changes state under a session cookie, so it must be covered by the app's CSRF defence, which depends on [OQ-2](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#5-open-questions). Worst case if missed: a user is mailed their own itinerary, up to the rate limit |
| Abuse | Email is capped by INV-5. The download has no ledger: it is bounded by auth, `RENDER_TIMEOUT` and `MAX_PDF_BYTES`, and otherwise relies on app-wide rate limiting, which does not exist yet |
| Privacy | No PDF is stored. Logs carry export id, user id, trip id, status, failure code, durations and PDF size. They never carry an email address or itinerary content |
| Reliability | Semantics are as stated in [SOURCE_OF_TRUTH §2](SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md#2-domain-model) and [§3.4](#34-email-export-flow). No automatic retry in v1 |
| Observability | One structured log line per export at close. Counters by status and failure code |
| Testing | Unit: renderer and message builder. Service: every failure code, with a fake `EmailSender`. Integration on real Postgres: each `CHECK`, the partial unique index, and two concurrent requests for INV-4 and INV-5 |
| Accessibility | Pending, success and failure states are announced, not only shown |

## Scope
Cloudflare Workers auth service (Hono + D1). Issues and validates session
tokens for POST /login, POST /logout, GET /session.

## Domain model
- `users` (D1): id, email, password_hash, created_at
- `sessions` (D1): id, user_id, token, expires_at

## Invariants
| # | Invariant | Enforced at |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Password hashes use scrypt, never stored plaintext | app layer (hash on write) + DB column has no plaintext default |
| 2 | A session token is single-use per refresh | app layer (rotate on use) + DB unique index on token |
| 3 | POST /login accepts at most 100 requests/min per client IP (best-effort, see ARCHITECTURE_ROADMAP.md §3.1); excess gets 429 before any D1 or scrypt work | app layer (Hono middleware ahead of the handler) + rate limit binding config (limit 100, period 60) |
